title: The Swellies (Chas McIvor)
style: country blues acoustic guitar warm baritone male vocal storytelling 102bpm walking bass brushed drums honest character portrait unhurried Perth ocean Rottnest
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Out past Rottnest Island where the swells come up from the south
Pete knows where the current turns and where to keep your mouth
About the conditions — some days you don't say a word
You just watch the water and you let the water be heard

[Pre-Chorus]
I called him once when the forecast showed a two-metre southern swell
He said he'd been out in four and it was fine — he could tell

[Chorus]
The swells come up from Antarctica without an explanation
They cross the Indian Ocean with considerable dedication
The swellies off the coast of Perth have run for two thousand miles
Before they meet a Pelican charter and Pete's nautical miles
That's my boy

[Verse 2]
The quokkas on the island don't concern themselves with swell
They're on the island and that's fine and everything is well
But out between the mainland and the reef on the blue
The swell is what the water says and Pete knows what to do

[Bridge]
My brother reads the ocean the way a carpenter reads grain
He ran his hand along the timber and he read the whole terrain
Now his hand is on the wheel and the ocean is the timber
And the Pelican runs true in December and in winter

[Outro]
The swellies know Pete's name now… the ocean knows Pete…
That's my boy
